name: Arakawa-Shakomae
tagline: Tokyo in 36 minutes and Otemachi in 39 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Arakawa City, where the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 39 minutes to Otemachi, 40 minutes to Shinjuku, 45 minutes to Shibuya and 50 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 2.6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 2.8 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 2.6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1.8 m to 4.6 m, a difference of 2.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of 3 to 5 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 3 to 5 m. For storm surge, 7 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the large side for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 10 clinics and 6 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 桑原病院, about 20 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 都立駒込病院, about 39 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line).
congestion: The ministry's congestion survey does not publish figures for Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line). It covers the major commuter stretches, and this line is not among them.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 2LDK ¥180,000 to ¥190,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. schools and parks within walking distance and quiet surroundings pushes the figure up. On the other side, a large projected flood depth and only one line, the {line}, serving the station holds it down.

neighbours.lead: For lower rent, Arakawa-Yuenchimae; for how close the centre is, Arakawa-Shakomae.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Arakawa-Shakomae. It is served by the same lines as Arakawa-Shakomae. To Shinjuku, for instance, Arakawa-Yuenchimae takes 3 minutes longer. A one-room flat costs about ¥7,000 less at Arakawa-Yuenchimae. On quiet, Arakawa-Shakomae comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: Oku is ahead on rail connections and how close the centre is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Arakawa-Shakomae. Oku also has the JR Utsunomiya Line and JR Takasaki Line, which Arakawa-Shakomae does not. With more lines, Oku is the better connected of the two. To Tokyo, for instance, Oku is 17 minutes quicker. A one-room flat also costs about ¥6,000 less at Oku.

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 7 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 4 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line) serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
